nodes.name: Webhook: Ingest
nodes.notes: POST {doc_id, text? | source_url?, metadata?}. Replies once, after the document is fully stored or has failed.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Embeddings, vector store and language model URLs, chunking, limits, tokens, and which hosts may be fetched. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Plan Ingest
nodes.notes: Checks auth (optional), CONFIG, and the document. A source_url is checked against ALLOWED_SOURCE_HOSTS and (when that is blank) refused if it points at localhost, a private network or a cloud metadata address.

nodes.name: Respond Ingest Early
nodes.notes: Replies to documents that stop early: 400, 401, 413, 415, 422, 500, 502 (source could not be fetched).

nodes.name: Fetch Source
nodes.notes: Fetches source_url (or passes the supplied text straight through). Redirects are followed by hand, up to 3, and every hop is re-checked against the host rules, so a public page cannot bounce the fetch to an internal address. Non-text content types are refused instead of being embedded as garbage.

nodes.name: Prepare Chunks
nodes.notes: Turns the page into clean text (HTML: scripts, styles and tags removed, entities decoded) and cuts it into overlapping chunks at paragraph, sentence or word boundaries instead of mid-word. The Playbook clean_rules run on the text before chunking. A document with no readable text is a 422 (the original had a 422 node that nothing was connected to).

nodes.name: Embed and Store
nodes.notes: THE INGEST ENGINE. Embeds every chunk (4 at a time, one retry each, early stop if the service is down, time budget), checks every vector, stores in batches with one retry, and only then removes leftover chunks from an older, longer version of the same document. Any failure is a 502 that says how many chunks were stored; the original answered "ingested" even when every embedding and upsert had failed.

nodes.name: Respond Ingest
nodes.notes: The single reply for a document that was worked on: 200 ingested, or 502 ingest_incomplete.

nodes.name: Expand Ingest Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. One Slack message per notice. Nothing if Slack is not configured. Text is escaped.

nodes.name: Send Ingest Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

nodes.name: Webhook: Delete
nodes.notes: POST {doc_id} with header x-delete-token. Removes every stored chunk of that document. Off (403) unless CONFIG.DELETE_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Is Delete?
nodes.notes: Delete requests skip the RAG Playbook on purpose, so a mistake in your playbook can never stop (or change) a delete.

nodes.name: Plan Delete
nodes.notes: Order: switch (403), token set and long enough (500), token matches (401), CONFIG (500), body (400). The token is a separate secret from the ingest token.

nodes.name: Respond Delete Early
nodes.notes: Replies to deletes that stop early: 400, 401, 403, 500.

nodes.name: Delete Document
nodes.notes: THE DELETE ENGINE. Counts the document's chunks (none = 404), deletes them by an exact doc_id filter, then counts again: it only replies "deleted" when zero chunks remain. Any failure is a 502 that says which step failed and is safe to retry. Ops get a Slack line for every delete and every failure.

nodes.name: Respond Delete
nodes.notes: The single reply for a delete that was attempted: 200 deleted, 404 doc_not_found, or 502 delete_incomplete.

nodes.name: Expand Delete Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. One Slack line for a delete (an audit trail) and one for each failure. Nothing if Slack is not configured. Text is escaped.

nodes.name: Send Delete Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

nodes.name: Webhook: Query
nodes.notes: POST {query, top_k?}. Replies with the answer and the sources it was based on.

nodes.name: Is Query?
nodes.notes: Both webhooks share the one CONFIG node, then split here.

nodes.name: RAG Playbook
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for client-specific behaviour: answer prompt and template, no-match message, text-cleaning rules, which metadata appears in sources and which can be filtered. Data only; the engine nodes check it on every request.

nodes.name: Plan Query
nodes.notes: Checks auth (optional), CONFIG, the Playbook, the question, top_k (clamped to 1..TOP_K_MAX) and optional metadata filters (only keys the Playbook lists as filterable).

nodes.name: Respond Query
nodes.notes: The reply for every query outcome: 200 answer, 200 no relevant documents, 400, 401, 500, 503 (embedding / vector store / model unavailable).

nodes.name: Search Knowledge Base
nodes.notes: Embeds the question and searches the vector store. An embedding or search failure is a 503 (the original reported it as "No relevant documents found", so an outage looked like an empty knowledge base). Results are re-sorted, de-duplicated, filtered by MIN_SCORE, and packed into a size-capped context where each chunk is wrapped in <document> tags.

nodes.name: Generate Answer
nodes.notes: Asks the model to answer from the supplied documents only. One retry. If the model is down or returns nothing, the caller gets a 503 that still includes the sources that were found. "cited" lists which retrieved documents the answer actually mentions.

parameters.content:
## RAG Knowledge Assistant
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 01-rag-knowledge-assistant-mock-server.js`, port 5200). It contains a **toy embedding model and a scripted stand-in for the language model**, not real ones.
2. Open **CONFIG** (one node serves both endpoints): point `EMBEDDINGS_API_URL` / `EMBEDDINGS_PATH` / `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `VECTOR_DB_URL` / `VECTOR_COLLECTION` (Qdrant-style API) and `LLM_API_URL` / `CHAT_MODEL` at your services. Set `INGEST_AUTH_TOKEN` and `QUERY_AUTH_TOKEN` before exposing it.
3. If you ingest from `source_url`, set `ALLOWED_SOURCE_HOSTS` (otherwise localhost, private networks and cloud metadata addresses are refused).
4. Activate. `POST /webhook/rag/ingest` with `{"doc_id":"handbook","text":"..."}`, then `POST /webhook/rag/query` with `{"query":"..."}`.

**Ingest:** validate -> fetch (optional) -> clean and chunk -> embed -> store -> remove leftovers of an older version. **Query:** validate -> embed -> search -> answer from the retrieved text only, with sources.
